title: 2015 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: A regular hexagon with sides of length \(6\) has an isosceles triangle attached to each side. Each of these triangles has two sides of length \(8.\) The isosceles triangles are folded to make a pyramid with the hexagon as the base of the pyramid. What is the volume of the pyramid?

solutions.text:
The distance from the hexagon’s center to a vertex is \(6.\) A lateral edge has length \(8,\) so the pyramid’s height is \(\sqrt{8^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{28} = 2\sqrt7.\)

The hexagon’s area is \(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}{2}\cdot 6^2 = 54\sqrt3.\) Thus the volume is \(\dfrac13 \cdot 54\sqrt3 \cdot 2\sqrt7 = 36\sqrt{21}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: In a regular hexagon of side \(6,\) the distance from the center to a vertex is also \(6\)
The apex sits above the center at height \(\sqrt{8^2 - 6^2};\) use \(V = \dfrac13 \cdot (\text{base area}) \cdot h\)
